result.title: There are now 80 machines for every human online
result.description:
Non-human identities, from bots to AI agents to Internet of Things devices, now massively outnumber people online. 

Many of these NHIs have authorization to carry out tasks on behalf of human users. But has security kept up with the pace of these new capabilities? Helmut Reisinger of @paloaltontwks discusses the challenge.

In the Global Cybersecurity Outlook 2026, 87% of leaders surveyed identified AI-related vulnerabilities as the fastest-growing cyber risk.

result.title: Your home could be powered by an electric car
result.description:
In the evening, power grids are under strain as millions of people switch on lights, appliances and air conditioners.
 
Meanwhile, fully charged electric cars sit idle, holding power that the grid needs.
 
A new technology called everything-to-grid energy is addressing this gap. It can turn vehicles, buildings and factories into nodes in a flexible, intelligent network that shares power with wherever it’s most needed. Electric vehicle owners receive money, utility bill credits or reduced financing costs in return. In developing regions, the technology could allow fleets of e-bikes or even agricultural tools to act as back-up power sources for the whole community.
 
Everything-to-grid has been selected as one of the World Economic Forum’s Top 10 Emerging Technologies of 2026.
 
#InnovateScaleImpact #AMNC26

result.title: Extreme Weather Prediction & Job Sectors Most at Risk from AI | WEF | Top Stories of the Week
result.description:
This week's top stories of the week include:

00:14 - Job sectors most at risk to AI: An entry-level job is usually the first stepping stone in a career. Today, however, AI is upending that paradigm. 37% of young workers around the world are in roles with a medium to high exposure to AI-driven #disruption. 

01.47 - Ageing populations are a benefit: How can society reframe #ageing away from narratives about fear, dependency and loss, and instead recognize the huge contributions that older people make? These are the questions at the forefront of George Wharton’s mind. Associate Professor of Health Policy at the London School of Economics, he works to bring about human-centred, coordinated care systems fit for an era in which, by 2030, 1 in 6 people will be 60 or over.


03.30 - Chinese city powers trucks using waste: Heavy trucks carry two-thirds of the world’s freight - and while they make up around 4% of the vehicles on our roads, they emit 11% of all transport emissions. The city of #Dalian is turning to #hydrogen fuel cells for trucks to ensure clean energy supply. 


04.51 - New AI predicts extreme weather: Faster, more accurate predictions about where a hurricane is going to hit can save lives. But existing weather prediction models tend to be expensive and slow, says Marvin Gabler, CEO of Jua. Now AI is stepping into this gap. Gabler explains how.

result.title: Ideas on the Move: Guo Jingjing
result.description:
Four Olympic golds. And her advice to young people: just go for it.

Diving champion Guo Jingjing joined us in Dalian for Ideas on the Move and reminded us that the fear of failure is usually the only thing standing in the way. Take the step. Learn from what happens. Try again.
